es: Reconocer preguntas retóricas, repetición, contraste y listas de tres en un discurso y nombrar el efecto que cada recurso tiene en el público.

teaching.en: Who will help our readers if the library closes?
teaching.es: ¿Quién ayudará a nuestros lectores si la biblioteca cierra?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta retórica: no espera respuesta, hace pensar al público. Tras if va el presente (closes), no will.
teaching.audioText: Who will help our readers if the library closes?

teaching.en: Books, shelves and volunteers: that is all we need.
teaching.es: Libros, estanterías y voluntarios: eso es todo lo que necesitamos.
teaching.explanationEs: Lista de tres: tres elementos seguidos dan ritmo y sensación de algo completo.
teaching.audioText: Books, shelves and volunteers: that is all we need.

teaching.en: We will fight for our readers. We will fight for our books. We will fight for our library.
teaching.es: Lucharemos por nuestros lectores. Lucharemos por nuestros libros. Lucharemos por nuestra biblioteca.
teaching.explanationEs: Repetición: la misma estructura al empezar cada frase fija la idea en la memoria.
segments: We will fight for our readers. We will fight
for our books. We will fight for our library.
teaching.audioText: We will fight for our readers. We will fight for our books. We will fight for our library.

teaching.en: The closure saves money today, but it costs us our future.
teaching.es: El cierre ahorra dinero hoy, pero nos cuesta el futuro.
teaching.explanationEs: Contraste: dos ideas opuestas unidas con but; el oyente ve la diferencia.
segments: The closure saves money today, but
teaching.audioText: The closure saves money today, but it costs us our future.

teaching.en: A rhetorical question makes the audience think; it does not wait for an answer.
teaching.es: Una pregunta retórica hace pensar al público; no espera una respuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Así se nombra el efecto: qué recurso es y qué provoca en quien escucha.
segments: A rhetorical question makes the audience think;
it does not wait for an answer.
teaching.audioText: A rhetorical question makes the audience think; it does not wait for an answer.

teaching.en: Repetition helps the audience remember the message.
teaching.es: La repetición ayuda al público a recordar el mensaje.
teaching.explanationEs: Otro efecto que conviene saber nombrar: la repetición hace que el mensaje se quede.
teaching.audioText: Repetition helps the audience remember the message.

prompt.es: ¿Qué recurso usa esta frase de un discurso?

choices.text: A list of three
A contrast
A rhetorical question

feedback.es: La frase termina en signo de pregunta, pero el orador no espera que nadie conteste: es una pregunta retórica.

hint.es: Termina en ? pero nadie espera contestar en voz alta.

origin.text: Who will listen to the children if we stay silent?

prompt.es: ¿Qué recurso domina este lema de un club de lectura?

choices.text: Repetition of the same pattern
A rhetorical question
A contrast between two ideas

feedback.es: Cada frase empieza igual (Read…): es una repetición de la misma estructura.

hint.es: Mira cómo empieza cada una de las tres frases.

origin.text: Read more. Read every day. Read with your friends.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Algunos ven un problema, pero nosotros vemos una oportunidad.»

answer.text: Some see a problem but we see a chance

feedback.es: Dos ideas opuestas, some people frente a we, se unen con but: eso crea el contraste.

hint.es: Primero la idea de los otros, luego but y la idea del orador.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y decide qué recurso domina.

choices.text: The speaker compares two opposite ideas.
The speaker repeats one pattern three times.
The speaker asks a question and waits.

feedback.es: Las tres frases empiezan con Every child needs: la misma estructura repetida fija el mensaje.

origin.audio: Every child needs a book. Every child needs a chance. Every child needs a library.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del discurso con el recurso que usa.

pairs: Who will clean this river if we do not?
It is small, but it is ours.
Fresh air, clean water, safe streets.
Clean rivers start here. Clean rivers start with us.

feedback.es: Cada frase tiene una marca distinta: signo de pregunta, but, tres elementos con comas o la misma estructura dos veces.

pairs: Who will clean this river if we do not?
It is small, but it is ours.
Fresh air, clean water, safe streets.
Clean rivers start here. Clean rivers start with us.

prompt.es: Completa: «La tienda es pequeña, pero su ayuda es grande.»

feedback.es: But une dos ideas opuestas (pequeña / grande): es el contraste que hace fuerte la frase.

origin.text: The shop is small, ___ its help is big.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace el orador en este fragmento.

choices.text: He asks two questions and then gives a warning.
He compares the past with the present.
He asks a question and then names three things the group has.

feedback.es: Primero hay una pregunta y después tres cosas que el grupo tiene: time, friends y plan.

origin.audio: Are we really going to wait? We have the time, we have the friends and we have the plan.

prompt.es: ¿Qué efecto busca esta pregunta en el público?

choices.text: It makes people think and find their own answer.
It gives the audience three facts to remember.
It shows that two ideas are opposite.

feedback.es: Una pregunta retórica no pide datos: invita a que cada persona llegue sola a la respuesta.

origin.text: Who wants to live in a town without a library?

prompt.es: Completa los nombres de dos recursos retóricos.

feedback.es: Rhetorical describe la pregunta que no espera respuesta, y repetition nombra el uso reiterado de las mismas palabras.

sentences: A question that needs no answer is a ___ question.
Using the same words again and again is called ___.

prompt.es: ¿Qué recurso aparece al final de este fragmento?

choices.text: It ends with two opposite ideas.
It ends with a question that needs no reply.
It ends by repeating the first words.

feedback.es: Después de la lista de tres elementos, el orador cierra con una pregunta que no busca respuesta.

origin.text: Clean air, safe roads, happy children. Is that too much to ask?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la idea que quiere transmitir el orador.

choices.text: Only old people need books.
Books are too expensive for the young.
Everyone should be able to read.

feedback.es: La repetición de books for… termina en everyone: el mensaje es que todos deben poder leer.

origin.audio: Books for the young, books for the old, books for everyone.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que contiene un contraste.

choices.text: The room is old, but the ideas inside it are new.
Who will fix the room if we do not?
Paper, pens and books: we have it all.

feedback.es: Old y new son ideas opuestas unidas por but. Las otras frases son una pregunta retórica y una lista.

prompt.es: Ordena la pregunta retórica: «¿Quién hablará por nosotros si no decimos nada?»

answer.text: Who will speak for us if we say nothing

feedback.es: Es una pregunta retórica: if + presente (say) y will en la pregunta principal.

title.en: What I need is, it was you who
title.es: Lo que necesito es, fuiste tú quien

es: Formar oraciones cleft con what, it y all para poner el foco en un dato: una cosa, una persona, un lugar o «lo único» que se quiere.

teaching.en: What worries the students is the noise in the old library.
teaching.es: Lo que preocupa a los estudiantes es el ruido de la vieja biblioteca.
teaching.explanationEs: What + verbo + is + dato: pone el foco en una cosa. Después de is va el dato destacado.
segments: What worries the students is the
teaching.audioText: What worries the students is the noise in the old library.

teaching.en: It was Sara who started the petition.
teaching.es: Fue Sara quien empezó la petición.
teaching.explanationEs: It was + persona + who + verbo: destaca quién lo hizo. Con personas, who.
teaching.audioText: It was Sara who started the petition.

teaching.en: All I want is a quiet place to study.
teaching.es: Lo único que quiero es un lugar tranquilo para estudiar.
teaching.explanationEs: All + sujeto + verbo + is: «lo único que». Sin what después de all.
teaching.audioText: All I want is a quiet place to study.

teaching.en: It is the volunteers who make the difference.
teaching.es: Son los voluntarios quienes marcan la diferencia.
teaching.explanationEs: El verbo de who concuerda con el dato destacado: volunteers, plural, por eso make.
teaching.audioText: It is the volunteers who make the difference.

teaching.en: What we did was write a letter to the mayor.
teaching.es: Lo que hicimos fue escribir una carta al alcalde.
teaching.explanationEs: Después de What we did was va el verbo en forma base: write, no wrote.
teaching.audioText: What we did was write a letter to the mayor.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo que me preocupa es el ruido.»

feedback.es: What + verbo + is abre la estructura «lo que…» y pone el foco en the noise.

hint.es: Es «lo que»: una palabra que empieza por W.

origin.text: ___ worries me is the noise.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál destaca a la persona: «Fue Sara quien empezó la petición»?

choices.text: It was Sara who started the petition.
What Sara started was the petition.
All Sara started was the petition.

feedback.es: Para destacar a una persona se usa it was + persona + who. Las otras dos ponen el foco en la petición, no en Sara.

hint.es: El dato destacado es Sara, no la petición.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lo único que quiero es un sitio tranquilo.»

answer.text: All I want is a quiet place

feedback.es: «Lo único que» se dice all + sujeto + verbo + is, sin what.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que quieren los estudiantes.

choices.text: More books.
More quiet rooms.
More computers.

feedback.es: El foco está después de is: more quiet rooms. La expresión not more books dice lo que no piden.

origin.audio: What the students want is more quiet rooms, not more books.

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue la alcaldesa quien respondió nuestra carta.»

feedback.es: Con una persona destacada se usa who (o that en inglés informal) seguido del verbo, sin repetir el sujeto.

origin.text: It was the mayor ___ answered our letter.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el dato que destaca.

pairs: It was Tom who wrote the letter.
It was in June that we met.
What they sent was a petition.
All I need is time.

feedback.es: Cada molde destaca algo distinto: it was + who una persona, it was + that un momento, what una cosa y all «lo único».

pairs: It was Tom who wrote the letter.
It was in June that we met.
What they sent was a petition.
All I need is time.

prompt.es: Escucha y decide quién dio la idea al hablante.

choices.text: The mayor gave him the idea.
A teacher gave him the idea.
Ana gave him the idea.

feedback.es: Lo que hizo el hablante fue llamar a la alcaldesa, pero quien le dio la idea fue Ana (It was Ana who…).

origin.audio: What I did was call the mayor. It was Ana who told me to do it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase destaca el lugar: «Nos conocimos en la biblioteca»?

choices.text: It was in the library that we met.
It was we who met in the library.
What we did was meet in the library.

feedback.es: Para destacar un lugar va it was + lugar + that. Las otras destacan las personas o la acción.

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue Tom…», «Lo que nos preocupa…», «Lo único que queremos…»

feedback.es: It was + persona + who destaca a Tom; What abre «lo que»; all o what sirven para «lo único que».

sentences: ___ was Tom who found the letter.
___ we want is a quiet room.

prompt.es: Reescribe la frase con un cleft que destaque a Leo.

answer.text: It was Leo who wrote the letter to the mayor.
accepted: It was Leo who wrote the letter to the mayor.
It was Leo that wrote the letter to the mayor.
It was Leo who wrote the mayor a letter.

feedback.es: Para destacar una persona se usa it was + persona + who + verbo: It was Leo who wrote…

origin.text: Leo wrote the letter to the mayor.

prompt.es: Elige el cleft que destaca lo que preocupa a Ana: el tráfico.

choices.text: It was the traffic who worried Ana.
What worries Ana is the traffic.
All worries Ana is the traffic.

feedback.es: What worries Ana is… destaca la cosa. Who no se usa con cosas y all necesita un sujeto antes del verbo.

origin.text: Ana worries about the traffic.

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue en junio cuando llegó la respuesta.»

feedback.es: Con un momento destacado, It was in June + that + verbo.

origin.text: It was in June ___ the answer arrived.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que pidieron.

choices.text: A lot of money.
A new building.
Just a short wait.

feedback.es: All they asked for was… marca «lo único que pidieron»: un poco de tiempo.

origin.audio: All they asked for was a little time.

es: Identificar la idea central, los recursos y el punto más débil de un discurso breve, y completar una ficha de análisis.

teaching.en: The candidate says that every student needs a voice.
teaching.es: La candidata dice que cada estudiante necesita una voz.
teaching.explanationEs: Idea central: lo que el orador quiere que creamos o hagamos.
teaching.audioText: The candidate says that every student needs a voice.

teaching.en: She repeats "Your voice, your vote" so that everyone remembers it.
teaching.es: Repite «Tu voz, tu voto» para que todos lo recuerden.
teaching.explanationEs: Recurso + efecto: la repetición sirve para que el mensaje se quede.
teaching.audioText: She repeats "Your voice, your vote" so that everyone remembers it.

teaching.en: Who will speak for your class if not your delegate?
teaching.es: ¿Quién hablará por tu clase si no lo hace tu delegado?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta retórica: no espera respuesta, hace pensar al público.
teaching.audioText: Who will speak for your class if not your delegate?

teaching.en: She makes a strong claim, but she gives no evidence.
teaching.es: Hace una afirmación fuerte, pero no da pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: Punto débil frecuente: una afirmación sin pruebas. Evidence no lleva -s.
teaching.audioText: She makes a strong claim, but she gives no evidence.

teaching.en: Her promises sound good, but she has no plan.
teaching.es: Sus promesas suenan bien, pero no tiene un plan.
teaching.explanationEs: Punto débil frecuente: una promesa sin plan para cumplirla.
teaching.audioText: Her promises sound good, but she has no plan.

teaching.en: The weak point of the speech is that she does not say how she will do it.
teaching.es: El punto débil del discurso es que no dice cómo lo hará.
teaching.explanationEs: En una pregunta indirecta no se invierte el orden: how she will do it.
segments: The weak point of the speech is that she
does not say how she will do it.
teaching.audioText: The weak point of the speech is that she does not say how she will do it.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la idea central de esta candidata?

choices.text: The class should have fewer lessons.
The class should have a place to relax and study.
The class should have longer breaks.

feedback.es: Después de «My idea is simple» está su tesis: un rincón tranquilo para leer, pensar y descansar.

hint.es: Busca la frase que sigue a «My idea is simple».

origin.text: My idea is simple. Every class needs a quiet corner. It will help us read, think and rest.

prompt.es: ¿Qué efecto tienen estas preguntas en el público?

choices.text: They give the audience three facts.
They show that two ideas are opposite.
They make the audience think about who can help.

feedback.es: Son preguntas retóricas: no piden datos, invitan a pensar quién puede ayudar, y la respuesta final es Only me.

hint.es: Nadie espera una respuesta real: la respuesta llega sola al final.

origin.text: Who else will listen to you? Who else will work for you? Only me.

prompt.es: Completa: «La candidata hace una afirmación fuerte, pero no da pruebas.»

feedback.es: Claim es la afirmación que el orador defiende; aquí no va acompañada de evidence.

hint.es: Es lo que se afirma: una «afirmación».

origin.text: The candidate makes a strong ___, but she gives no evidence.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la idea central de Leo.

choices.text: Students should help to decide the school rules.
Students should have fewer rules.
Students should stay out of school decisions.

feedback.es: La frase I believe that… presenta la idea central: los estudiantes deben ayudar a decidir las normas.

origin.audio: Hello, everyone. My name is Leo and I want to be your delegate. I believe that students should help to make the school rules. Vote for a school that listens.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es el punto débil de este fragmento?

choices.text: It does not say what the speaker wants.
It makes a strong claim without any evidence.
It uses a list of three facts.

feedback.es: Se afirma que es la escuela más ruidosa de la ciudad y nadie da pruebas. Sí se entiende lo que el orador quiere.

origin.text: Our school is the noisiest in the city. Everybody knows it. Vote for me and I will change it.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su lugar en la ficha de análisis.

pairs: Our school needs a bigger playground.
Who else will speak for you?
I promise a perfect school!
Your voice, your vote.

feedback.es: La idea central dice qué se defiende; la pregunta retórica y la repetición son recursos; una promesa sin plan es un punto débil.

pairs: Our school needs a bigger playground.
Who else will speak for you?
I promise a perfect school!
Your voice, your vote.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que propone Nora.

choices.text: She wants longer lunch breaks.
She wants free trips for the class.
She wants to improve the food at lunch.

feedback.es: Nora dice que la clase necesita better lunches: propone mejorar la comida. Ella hace una pregunta retórica, pero su idea central es esa.

origin.audio: Hello, I am Nora. I want to be your delegate because our class needs better lunches. Do you want the same food every day? I do not! Vote for better lunches.

prompt.es: ¿Qué punto débil tiene este discurso?

choices.text: It makes promises but does not say who will pay.
It has no clear main point.
It uses too many rhetorical questions.

feedback.es: Promete muchas cosas gratis sin explicar quién las pagará: promesas sin plan.

origin.text: I promise new computers for every student, a pool for the school and a trip to Paris. It will all be free. Trust me.

prompt.es: Completa la ficha de análisis del discurso.

feedback.es: La idea central es el huerto, el recurso es la pregunta retórica y falta un plan para construirlo.

sentences: Main point: our class needs a ___.
Weak point: no ___ for the garden.
origin.text: Who else will speak for you? Our class needs a garden, and I will build it. Trust me.

prompt.es: Escribe la idea central y el punto débil de este discurso.

answer.text: The main point is that every student needs a voice. The weak point is that Ben does not say how he will do it.
accepted: The main point is that every student needs a voice. The weak point is that Ben does not say how he will do it.
Ben says that every student needs a voice. The weak point is that he has no plan for the clubs.
The main point is that students need a voice. The problem is that Ben gives no plan for the new clubs.

feedback.es: Una buena ficha nombra la idea central (every student needs a voice) y el punto débil: promete clubes pero no explica cómo.

origin.text: Hello! I am Ben. Every student needs a voice. Who will listen to your ideas? I will. I promise a new club every month, but I do not say how.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué recurso usa el candidato.

choices.text: He compares two opposite ideas.
He asks questions that need no answer.
He lists three facts.

feedback.es: Las dos primeras frases son preguntas que no esperan respuesta: pregunta retórica, con la respuesta al final.

origin.audio: Who will speak for you? Who will work for you? Vote for Tom, and Tom will.

choices.text: A clear call to vote.
A main point.
Evidence to support his claim.

feedback.es: Sam afirma que tiene las mejores ideas, pero no da ninguna prueba. Sí pide el voto y su idea central es ser el mejor delegado.

origin.text: Hello! Vote for Sam. Sam has the best ideas and Sam will be the best delegate. Trust him.

es: Redactar un párrafo persuasivo para defender un huerto escolar o un club de lectura con una pregunta retórica, un cleft y un contraste.

teaching.en: Who would say no to fresh vegetables grown by our own students?
teaching.es: ¿Quién diría que no a verduras frescas cultivadas por nuestros propios estudiantes?
teaching.explanationEs: Gancho: una pregunta retórica al principio atrapa al lector. Nadie responde que no.
segments: Who would say no to fresh
vegetables grown by our own students?
teaching.audioText: Who would say no to fresh vegetables grown by our own students?

teaching.en: The garden costs little, but it teaches a lot.

teaching.explanationEs: Contraste: el coste contra el beneficio. Con un nombre incontable (little), nunca few.
teaching.audioText: The garden costs little, but it teaches a lot.

teaching.en: What makes a garden special is that every student can help.
teaching.es: Lo que hace especial a un huerto es que todos los estudiantes pueden ayudar.

segments: What makes a garden special is
teaching.audioText: What makes a garden special is that every student can help.

teaching.en: It was the volunteers who built the first beds last spring.

segments: It was the volunteers who built
teaching.audioText: It was the volunteers who built the first beds last spring.

teaching.en: Plant, learn and share: that is what our garden offers.

teaching.audioText: Plant, learn and share: that is what our garden offers.

teaching.en: Join us, and you will see the difference.
teaching.es: Únete a nosotros y verás la diferencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Llamada a la acción: una orden amable al final invita a participar.
teaching.audioText: Join us, and you will see the difference.

prompt.es: Completa el gancho: «¿Quién diría que no a un club donde todos leen juntos?»

feedback.es: Una pregunta retórica sobre personas empieza con Who: nadie respondería que sí a decir que no.

hint.es: Es una pregunta sobre personas: empieza por W.

origin.text: ___ would say no to a club where everyone reads together?

prompt.es: Ordena el contraste: «Cuesta poco, pero enseña mucho.»

answer.text: It costs little but it teaches a lot

accepted: Who would say no to a school garden? It costs little, but it teaches a lot. What makes it special is that every student can help. Plant, learn and share: join us!
Who would say no to a reading club? It costs little, but it gives a lot. What matters is that everyone can join. Read, talk and share: join us!
Who would not want a school garden? The garden is small, but the students learn a lot. It was the students who planted it. Come and join us!

feedback.es: Un buen párrafo abre con una pregunta retórica, contrasta coste y beneficio y destaca lo esencial con un cleft.

origin.text: Elige un huerto o un club de lectura. Usa una pregunta retórica, un cleft (What… is / It was… who) y un contraste (…, but…). Ideas: cuesta poco, enseña mucho, todos pueden participar.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la pregunta retórica más natural para abrir un párrafo sobre el club?

choices.text: Who would say no to a club where everyone reads?
Who said no to the club yesterday?
Is the club open on Mondays?

feedback.es: Una pregunta retórica no pide datos: todos saben que nadie diría que no. Las otras dos piden información real.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo que hace especial al huerto es que todos pueden ayudar.»

feedback.es: What makes… is that + oración: así se cierra el cleft, sin because.

origin.text: What makes the garden special ___ that everyone can help.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige quién pidió el club de lectura.

choices.text: The students made the request.
Some teachers made the request.
The mayor made the request.

feedback.es: It was the teachers who… destaca a los profesores como autores de la petición.

origin.audio: It was the teachers who asked for a reading club. What they wanted was a quiet place for books.

es: Lanzar una campaña breve: leer datos, crear un lema, redactar un mensaje con recursos retóricos variados y responder a una objeción con tono adecuado.

teaching.en: Our school throws away four hundred plastic bottles every week.
teaching.es: Nuestro colegio tira cuatrocientas botellas de plástico cada semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Un dato concreto da fuerza al mensaje: cifra + qué + periodo. Four hundred no lleva -s.
teaching.audioText: Our school throws away four hundred plastic bottles every week.

teaching.en: Our slogan is short: bring your own bottle.
teaching.es: Nuestro lema es corto: trae tu propia botella.
teaching.explanationEs: Un buen lema es breve, fácil de repetir y empieza con un verbo.
teaching.audioText: Our slogan is short: bring your own bottle.

teaching.en: Who wants to see the playground full of plastic?
teaching.es: ¿Quién quiere ver el patio lleno de plástico?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta retórica: engancha al público con una imagen que nadie desea.
teaching.audioText: Who wants to see the playground full of plastic?

teaching.en: What this campaign needs is your help.
teaching.es: Lo que necesita esta campaña es tu ayuda.
teaching.explanationEs: Cleft con What: destaca la petición principal antes de pedirla.
teaching.audioText: What this campaign needs is your help.

teaching.en: I understand your concern, but a good bottle lasts for years.
teaching.es: Entiendo tu preocupación, pero una buena botella dura años.
teaching.explanationEs: Responder a una objeción: reconoce primero (I understand), contrasta con but y da un dato.
segments: I understand your concern, but a
teaching.audioText: I understand your concern, but a good bottle lasts for years.

teaching.en: Your objection is fair, but the numbers are clear.
teaching.es: Tu objeción es razonable, pero las cifras son claras.
teaching.explanationEs: Otra forma de empezar la respuesta: acepta lo justo y vuelve a los datos.
teaching.audioText: Your objection is fair, but the numbers are clear.

prompt.es: ¿Qué lema encaja con esta campaña?

choices.text: Fill it, carry it, reuse it.
Use it once, then forget it.
Less water, more plastic.

feedback.es: El lema debe coincidir con la acción de la campaña: rellenar y reutilizar la botella. Las otras opciones defienden lo contrario.

hint.es: Piensa en lo que hace cada estudiante con su botella.

origin.text: Campaign: each student brings a bottle from home and fills it at the school fountain.

prompt.es: Completa la respuesta: «Entiendo tu preocupación, pero una buena botella dura años.»

feedback.es: La respuesta reconoce la objeción y la contrasta con but antes de dar el dato.

hint.es: Reconoces una idea y la contrastas con otra.

origin.text: I understand your concern, ___ a good bottle lasts for years.

answer.text: Bring your bottle and make a big difference

feedback.es: Un lema empieza con un verbo (bring) y une dos acciones con and.

hint.es: Empieza con el verbo de la orden.

prompt.es: Escucha y calcula cuántas botellas tira el colegio cada día.

choices.text: About 400.
About 80.
About 40.

feedback.es: Cuatrocientas botellas a la semana son unas ochenta al día, como dice la frase final.

feedback.es: What + verbo + is pone el foco en lo que se pide.

origin.text: What this campaign needs ___ your help.

choices.text: You are right, so we will stop the campaign.
That is a bad idea and nobody agrees with you.

feedback.es: Reconoce la objeción (I see your point) y la contrasta con but. Una respuesta que se rinde o que ataca no convence.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué recursos combina el orador.

choices.text: A list of three and a rhetorical question.
A contrast and a repeated pattern.
A cleft and a list of two.

feedback.es: Hay tres lugares con plástico y una pregunta final que no espera respuesta.

origin.audio: Plastic in the river, plastic in the sea, plastic on our plates. Is that the future we want?

prompt.es: Completa: «Fueron los estudiantes…», «Lo que nos preocupa…», «Lo único que pedimos…»

feedback.es: It was + personas + who destaca a los autores, What abre «lo que» y all… is marca «lo único».

sentences: ___ was the students who wrote the slogan.
___ worries us is the waste in the bins.
All we ask for ___ one small change.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es el punto débil de este discurso?

choices.text: It has no clear main point.
It promises a lot but gives no plan or evidence.
It uses too many questions.

feedback.es: Promete resultados enormes en un mes sin explicar cómo ni dar pruebas.

origin.text: Join our campaign! In one month, every student will have a bottle, every bin will be empty and every river will be clean. It will be easy.

prompt.es: Lanza la campaña: lema, mensaje con tres recursos y respuesta a una objeción.

answer.text: Our slogan: bring your own bottle! Every week our school throws away 400 plastic bottles. Who wants to see that plastic in the river? It is a small change, but it makes a big difference. What matters is that every student can join. Some say bottles are expensive. I understand your concern, but a good bottle lasts for years.
accepted: Our slogan: bring your own bottle! Every week our school throws away 400 plastic bottles. Who wants to see that plastic in the river? It is a small change, but it makes a big difference. What matters is that every student can join. Some say bottles are expensive. I understand your concern, but a good bottle lasts for years.

Our slogan is: fill it, carry it, reuse it! Our school throws away four hundred plastic bottles every week. Who wants a playground full of plastic? What we need is one small change. Some students say a bottle is expensive, but there are twelve fountains and a good bottle lasts for years. I see your point, but we can all help.

Bring your own bottle is our slogan. Every week the school wastes 400 plastic bottles. Who would like to see them in the river? It was the students who found this problem, and it is the students who can change it. I understand your concern, but a good bottle lasts for years.

feedback.es: Una campaña completa reúne el dato, un lema, tres recursos variados y una respuesta que reconoce la objeción y la contrasta con un dato.
